questions.stem: What are the two basic building blocks of a graph?
options: Vertices (nodes) and edges (links)
Rows and columns
Tables and keys
Files and folders
Classes and objects
questions.explanation: A graph is made up of dots called vertices (or nodes) and lines called edges (or links) that connect them.

questions.stem: What is the correct use of the terms 'vertex' and 'vertices'?
options: Vertex means an edge, vertices means many edges
One node is called a vertex; multiple nodes are called vertices
Vertex is the plural of vertices
Both terms refer only to directed graphs
Vertex means a weighted node
questions.explanation: One node is called a vertex whereas multiple nodes are called vertices.

questions.stem: In which type of graph do the edges have a direction, shown by arrows?
options: Undirected graph
Simple graph
Directed graph (digraph)
Complete graph
Bipartite graph
questions.explanation: In a directed graph, or digraph, the edges have a direction shown by arrows; in an undirected graph the connection works both ways.

options: A graph in which every point is connected to every other point
A graph with no loops or duplicate edges
A graph whose vertices are split into two groups
A graph whose edges carry values or weights, such as distance or cost
A graph with no cycles
questions.explanation: In a weighted graph the edges have values or weights, like distance or cost.

questions.stem: Which type of graph has every point connected to every other point?
options: Simple graph
Bipartite graph
Tree
Directed graph
Complete graph
questions.explanation: A complete graph is one in which every point is connected to every other point.

questions.stem: In a bipartite graph, how are the points and lines arranged?
options: The points are split into two groups and lines only connect points from different groups
Every point is connected to every other point
All lines start and end at the same point
The points form a single cycle
Each point has exactly one edge
questions.explanation: A bipartite graph splits the points into two groups, and lines only connect points from different groups.

questions.stem: What does the degree of a vertex measure?
options: The angle between two edges
The number of edges connected to that point
The distance to the farthest vertex
The weight of the heaviest edge
The number of cycles in the graph
questions.explanation: Degree is the number of edges connected to a point; in a directed graph this splits into in-degree and out-degree.

questions.stem: In a directed graph, what is the in-degree of a vertex?
options: The number of edges pointing away from the vertex
The total number of vertices in the graph
The number of edges pointing to the vertex
The number of loops at the vertex
The weight of the vertex
questions.explanation: In-degree counts the edges pointing to a vertex, while out-degree counts the edges pointing away from it.

questions.stem: What is a cycle in a graph?
options: Any two vertices connected by an edge
A graph with no edges
A vertex with degree zero
A path that starts and ends at the same point
An edge with a weight of zero
questions.explanation: A cycle is a path that starts and ends at the same point.

questions.stem: What is a tree in graph terms?
options: A graph in which every edge is weighted
A graph with exactly one cycle
A graph whose vertices fall into two groups
A graph that is disconnected
A special type of graph that is connected and has no cycles
questions.explanation: A tree is a special type of graph that is connected and has no cycles.
